reasons: The tests were read, not run, so passing status is not confirmed.
Error message matching makes some tests sensitive to library wording changes.

terms.meaning: a reference example used to check the pipeline gives expected results
a ranking of how official a piece of evidence is, where a lower number means more authoritative
a shared capability that several processes depend on, identified by a fixed code
the identifier that lets the system find a case by its folder and name

used_by: the pytest run for the schema tests

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and background
sections.what: Imports the case contract, the manifest tiers and the test tools. The docstring records that the contract once checked only key names.
sections.why: The docstring explains why the validation is now much stricter.

sections.name: lending
sections.title: Loading the lending golden case
sections.what: Reads the commercial lending golden input from disk and returns it as plain data.
sections.why: Many tests start from a known good case and change one part.
sections.watch_out: If that folder is renamed, every test that uses it fails with a file-not-found error.

sections.name: case
sections.title: Building a case with overrides
sections.what: Validates the lending case with the given top-level fields replaced, raising an error if the result is invalid.
sections.why: Lets one test check one bad field without changing the rest.

sections.name: with_process
sections.title: Building a case with process overrides
sections.what: Like the case builder, but replaces fields inside the process section.
sections.why: Volume and process fields sit inside that section, so tests need a way to change them.
sections.watch_out: Only the keys given are replaced, so the rest of the process section keeps its lending values.

sections.name: TestTheGoldenSetSatisfiesIt
sections.title: Golden cases are valid and in place
sections.what: Checks there are exactly four golden cases, that each one validates, and that each one sits in the folder matching its canonical id and industry.
sections.why: If the list shrank to zero, the per-case checks would vanish without failing. The count test guards against that.
sections.watch_out: The count of four is fixed, so adding a case means changing this number.

sections.name: TestTheFailuresThatUsedToLoad (part 1)
sections.title: Bad inputs that used to load
sections.what: Each test shows a bad input is now refused: a misspelt depth tier, an inverted or negative volume, a text or out-of-range authority tier, an unknown enabler, an unknown prerequisite kind, a duplicate evidence id, and an undeclared extra field.
sections.why: Each of these used to pass the old key-presence check and then fail deep inside a run, or silently skew results.
sections.watch_out: The extra-field test accepts two phrasings of the error, which depends on the validation library's wording.

sections.name: TestTheFailuresThatUsedToLoad: test_an_empty_exercises_list_is_refused
sections.title: Empty list and missing date refused
sections.what: Refuses an empty exercises list and a missing published date, and accepts a date that is explicitly set to nothing.
sections.why: An absent date and a deliberately undated item are different statements, and only the second is a real result.

sections.name: TestDirectoryCorrespondence
sections.title: Folder placement is checked
sections.what: Checks that a canonical id that does not match its folder is reported, that an industry mismatch is reported, and that a matching case reports no problems.
sections.why: A case in the wrong folder would not be found by discovery.

sections.name: TestTheContractStaysAlignedWithTheRunManifest
sections.title: Staying aligned with the run manifest
sections.what: Checks that the depth tiers match the run manifest, that the enabler vocabulary matches the pattern library, and that prerequisite kinds come from the shared enumeration.
sections.why: The depth tier list is declared in two places, so this test keeps them the same.
sections.watch_out: The enabler test checks one fixed sample code, so changing the sample case means updating this test.

sections.name: TestWhatTheContractDeliberatelyPermits
sections.title: Allowances the contract permits on purpose
sections.what: Confirms an empty evidence pack, negative earnings, free-text work unit, and an absent headcount are all accepted, and that authority tiers are ordered from most to least authoritative.
sections.why: Each allowance is a deliberate choice with a reason stated in the docstrings.
sections.watch_out: Tightening any of these rules would reject legitimate cases the docstrings describe.

summary: Tests the input contract for golden cases, covering each rule and each kind of bad input that used to load and then fail deep inside a run.
purpose: Makes sure every golden case is valid, sits in the right folder, and that bad input is refused at load time with a clear error.
why: The module docstring says the older contract only checked that keys were present, so bad values loaded and failed later. The tests now cover each case that used to slip through.
how: Reads the lending golden case from disk, applies small changes to it, and checks that validation accepts or refuses the result. Separate groups check the golden set itself, the failures, the folder placement, alignment with the run manifest, and the deliberate allowances.
inputs: The lending golden case file under evals/golden, plus changed copies built in the tests.
outputs: Pass or fail results from pytest. No files are written.
risks: The count of four golden cases is fixed in the test, so adding a case requires updating it. Some tests check exact error wording.
debug: If a golden case fails validation, open its input file and check the field named in the error. If the folder test fails, check that the case sits in the folder matching its id and industry.
